input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 satisfies our preferred position on all material terms and comfortably clears the fallback. The cap is expressly mutual ("The cap is mutual"), set at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000; "Fees" (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the basis is not illusory. Section 21.2 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually (and helpfully confirms data restoration, replacement services, notices and incident response are direct damages). Section 21.3's Excluded Claims sit outside the cap and cover confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's IP. Section 21.4 preserves liability that cannot lawfully be limited and survives failure of an exclusive remedy. No competing or one-sided cap appears elsewhere (the only other "liability" references are Vendor's insurance covenants in §18.1). The one shortfall from preferred wording is that the payment carve-out in §21.3 is limited to "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" rather than all Customer amounts due; that narrowing operates in our favour (it keeps disputed and non-Fee amounts inside the cap rather than exposing us to uncapped payment claims), so we note it rather than redline it. No redline proposed.
